SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Reading 5.2.1 Pre- reading, part of Time Suggested vocabulary morning, afternoon, evening, night, day, late, early,  in SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade one General.

Key inquiry question: Why do we learn sounds?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Reading 5.2.1 Pre- reading together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Communication and Collaboration: learner’s team work spirit is enhanced as they contribute to group decision making by recognizing the

value of other’s ideas during group activities.

• Digital literacy: learner’s ability to interact with digital technology is enhanced as they engage in letter matching activities in digital format.

Values:
Unity: is enhanced as the learner strives to achieve common goals in group and pair activities.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
Life skills: Self-esteem is promoted as learners develop confidence in their reading competency.

Links to other Learning Areas:
Kiswahili Language Activities: as learners further their reading skills facilitate knowledge acquisition through the role of letter- sound

correspondence for reading preparedness.

Suggested Learning Resources:

Pocket charts/digital flash cards/ charts/flash cards, assistive technology such as universal cuffs/wrist braces/arm braces, weighted pencil/pen

grips, page-turners, adapted digital devices with filter keys/key guards/larger mouse/head control input devices such as head wand
